annotation.title_clean: Commission Staff Working Document Impact Assessment Report accompanying the Proposal for a Directive on adapting non-contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence
annotation.title_en: Commission Staff Working Document Impact Assessment Report accompanying the Proposal for a Directive on adapting non-contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence
annotation.summary_en: Commission impact assessment for the proposed AI Liability Directive. It identifies legal uncertainty, fragmentation and victim under-compensation caused by AI opacity and autonomy, compares three options (easing burden of proof; plus strict liability and insurance; staged approach), and prefers the staged approach. It uses cleaning robots, drones and vehicles as examples.
key_provisions_or_claims: AI opacity, autonomy and complexity make fault and causation hard for victims to prove
PO1: court-ordered disclosure of evidence and rebuttable presumption of causality tied to AI Act non-compliance
PO2 adds strict liability and possibly mandatory insurance for specific high-risk AI uses
PO3 staged approach (PO1 now, targeted review of strict liability and insurance later) is preferred
Initiative complements the AI Act and the Product Liability Directive revision under Article 114 TFEU
